blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — ephedrine tachyphylaxis during treatment of anesthesia-related hypotension
stem: A client with anesthesia-related hypotension receives repeated IV ephedrine boluses. The nurse notices that later doses produce a smaller pressor response than earlier doses. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: Repeated ephedrine can produce tachyphylaxis, so the pressor response may progressively diminish and an alternative pressor may be needed if responsiveness becomes inadequate.
options.B: Repeated ephedrine should produce an unchanged response because it acts only as a direct alpha-1 agonist and has no indirect norepinephrine-releasing activity.
options.C: A weaker pressor response is expected because ephedrine is primarily a direct vasodilator whose vascular relaxation increases progressively with repeated bolus dosing.
options.D: The diminished response indicates an immediate allergic reaction to ephedrine rather than a pharmacologic tolerance phenomenon associated with repeated administration.

rationale: Current ephedrine sulfate injection labeling identifies ephedrine as an alpha- and beta-adrenergic agonist and a norepinephrine-releasing agent. The label specifically warns that repeated administration may cause tachyphylaxis and advises clinicians to be prepared with an alternative pressor when responsiveness becomes unacceptable. Therefore A is correct. B misstates the mechanism, C reverses the drug's pressor action, and D assigns an unsupported diagnosis to a labeled tolerance phenomenon.
educational_objective: Recognize tachyphylaxis as a cause of diminishing pressor response after repeated IV ephedrine and understand the drug's mixed alpha/beta and norepinephrine-releasing activity.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_document_title: EPHEDRINE SULFATE injection — Full Prescribing Information
source_version_date: Prescribing information revised June 2026; current DailyMed label published 2026 and accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Indications and Usage §1: alpha- and beta-adrenergic agonist and norepinephrine-releasing agent for clinically important anesthesia-related hypotension. Warnings and Precautions §5.2 Tachyphylaxis and Tolerance: repeated administration may cause tachyphylaxis; be prepared with an alternative pressor if responsiveness becomes unacceptable.
source_claim_supported: Ephedrine has mixed alpha/beta adrenergic and norepinephrine-releasing activity, and repeated administration can cause tachyphylaxis with a progressively reduced pressor response.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate medication response; recognize altered therapeutic effect; safely manage IV vasoactive medications.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices without absolute-word distractor cues.
Balanced option length and retained the exact labeled tachyphylaxis concept and mixed sympathomimetic mechanism.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current June 2026 ephedrine labeling. No absolute-word cue or second defensible answer remains.
